timing: after a 4-case technical smoke run (ref_ACB, ref_ACI, ref_BBAI, ref_OPTX) and before the full B1 run. Disclosed as a post-hoc clarification; it does not change any decision criterion, only how a re-fetched document is compared with its V9 citation.
finding: www.sec.gov injects a per-request bot-manager tag '<script type="text/javascript"  src="/<random path>"></script>' right before '</body>' into complete HTML documents. The random path changes length and content on every request, so the sha256 of a complete re-fetched body never reproduces the V9 sha256 (example: acb-20210630.htm V9 926298 bytes, now 926288 bytes, identical apart from that tag). Prefix reads that stop before '</body>' are unaffected.

changes.rule: Q-INT.validFrom re-verification of the V9 start document
changes.after: re-verify the content: the fresh body must again contain the V9 evidence (iXBRL cover row with the ticker and a COMMON class title, or a venue-checked ticker statement). The record cites the fresh body with sha256 (raw) and sha256Normalized (bot-manager tag removed); 'v9Sha256Reproduced' says whether the raw V9 sha256 was reproduced. A missing V9 start document remains START_DOCUMENT_NOT_REVERIFIED.

every cited complete HTML body additionally carries sha256Normalized = sha256(body with the trailing bot-manager script tag removed, regex <script type="text/javascript"\s+src="/[^"]*"></script>(?=</body>)). The independent check verifies sha256Normalized.
